target.title: fix(google): add timeout to Vertex ADC token refresh
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Google Vertex Application Default Credentials refresh could wait indefinitely. The custom `authorized_user` OAuth path had no request deadline, and library-managed ADC sources such as Workload Identity Federation or GCE/GKE metadata could also leave OpenClaw waiting forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The custom OAuth refresh now uses the shared 30-second abort deadline across both response headers and bounded body consumption.
- The `google-auth-library` fallback has an owner-level 30-second deadline. This is necessary because the pinned library uses separate transports for some STS and metadata refresh paths, so configuring its top-level Gaxios transporter would not cover every ADC source.
- Timeout proof is folded into the existing Google transport suite; the 205-line private TCP harness and its test-only production seam were removed.

Credential discovery, token caching, response-size limits, gzip handling, and error parsing are unchanged. No config or environment surface was added.

## User Impact

Vertex authentication failures now return within 30 seconds instead of leaving provider work stuck indefinitely, including `authorized_user` refresh and library-managed ADC resolution.

## Collision / Differentiation Check

- #98507 bounds token response body size; this PR bounds refresh duration.
- #101035 concerns project environment resolution.
- #91222 concerns retry behavior after pre-stream failures.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `2cc02c4f41d35d530e0754fbd781f10eca1a6f29`
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox (`aws`, lease `cbx_9013e7de2edc`, run `run_3acff6e93db3`): `pnpm test extensions/google/transport-stream.test.ts` — 1 file, 85 tests passed.
- Fresh structured autoreview: clean.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

Mutation proof: the focused tests hang without the corresponding deadline and reject with `TimeoutError` when the production deadline is restored.

Google contracts checked: [OAuth refresh-token flow](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/web-server#offline) and [Application Default Credentials](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials).

Not tested: a live Google OAuth, Workload Identity, or Vertex tenant; no live ADC credentials were available. The deterministic tests cover both the custom fetch path and the `google-auth-library` owner boundary.
